body:
## Summary

Fixes the `ci-caipe-ui` workflow failure that occurs when documentation-only changes are merged to `main`.

**Root Cause:**
- The `ci-caipe-ui.yml` workflow triggers on any changes to `ui/**` paths (including docs)
- The `rc-tag.yml` workflow only triggers on code changes (`ai_platform_engineering/**`, `build/**`, etc.)
- When docs-only PRs merge, `ci-caipe-ui` waits for an RC tag that never comes, causing failure

**Solution:**
- Updated `determine-release-tag` action to handle missing RC tag runs gracefully
- Instead of failing, it now exits successfully and proceeds with `latest` tag
- Added informative messages explaining this is expected behavior for non-release changes

## Changes

- Modified `.github/actions/determine-release-tag/action.yml`:
  - Changed exit code from `1` to `0` when no RC tag workflow is found
  - Added clear messaging about expected behavior
  - Allows workflow to proceed with empty tag (defaults to `latest`)

## Testing

This fix addresses the failure seen in:
- Run: https://github.com/cnoe-io/ai-platform-engineering/actions/runs/21396443979
- PR #713 (docs-only changes that still triggered UI workflow)

## Impact

- ✅ Documentation PRs will no longer fail CI unnecessarily
- ✅ UI builds will still succeed with `latest` tag for docs changes
- ✅ RC tagging workflow continues to work normally for code changes
- ✅ No breaking changes to existing behavior

## Related

- Closes the issue with PR #713's failing CI
- Improves developer experience for documentation contributions

### [`v1.34.1`](https://redirect.github.com/meilisearch/meilisearch/releases/tag/v1.34.1)

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/meilisearch/meilisearch/compare/v1.34.0...v1.34.1)

In Meilisearch v1.34.1, we released a security fix that affect web queries initiated by Meilisearch.

##### 🔐 Security

- Cloud users: no action is needed. We found no evidence of exploitation on Meilisearch Cloud and the Cloud is protected at the infrastructure level.
- Open-source users: if you allow untrusted users to configure webhooks, embedders or network of machines, we recommend you update to Meilisearch v1.34.1

In Meilisearch versions v1.8 to v1.34.0, a user with an API key with *write permissions* to the configuration of the Meilisearch instance could set up Meilisearch to send POST or GET requests to domains and IPs local to the private network of the Meilisearch instance, effectively bypassing the firewall. The vulnerability has not yet been assigned a CVE number; it has CVE Request [`1975471`](https://redirect.github.com/meilisearch/meilisearch/commit/1975471) for CVE ID.

Meilisearch v1.34.1 fixes the vulnerability by forbidding Meilisearch from making any requests to a host resolving to a non-global IP, in the sense of the [IANA IPv4 Special-Purpose Address Registry](https://www.iana.org/assignments/iana-ipv4-special-registry/iana-ipv4-special-registry.xhtml) or the [IANA IPv6 Special-Purpose Address Registry](https://www.iana.org/assignments/iana-ipv6-special-registry/iana-ipv6-special-registry.xhtml). If you need this functionality in your Meilisearch instance, you can set private IP networks as allowed with the `--experimental-allow-ip-networks` parameter after reviewing the security implications.

**This is a breaking change**, which is allowed for security reasons.

author: micmarty-deepsense
body:
## Problem

When `OTEL_TRACES_EXPORTER=none` or `OTEL_METRICS_EXPORTER=none` is set, plugin pods crash on startup with:

### Real-world scenario
In in-vpc or single-node clusters, you might notice this issue in plugin pods (created by the job-execution-operator) when you set those environment variables in the `JOB_ENV_VARS` block.

https://github.com/Unstructured-IO/platform-applications-cd/blob/9cf7335f3fe620106c61da208c12d44539d743bc/apps/dataplane/etl-operator/values.yaml#L52

```
NotImplementedError: none implementation not supported yet
```

**Root cause:** The code splits the env var by comma but doesn't filter "none", then tries to initialize exporters for it, hitting the `NotImplementedError` in `_add_trace_exporter()` and `_get_metrics_reader()`.

## Solution

### 1. Filter "none" from exporter lists (lines 33, 37)
```python
trace_exporters = [e for e in trace_exporters if e != "none"]
metric_exporters = [e for e in metric_exporters if e != "none"]
```

### 2. Return None when no exporters configured (lines 45-49, 59-63)
```python
def get_trace_provider() -> TracerProvider | None:
    settings = get_settings()
    if not settings["trace_exporters"]:
        return None  # Let OTEL SDK use default no-op
    ...
```

## Compatibility

`FastAPIInstrumentor.instrument_app()` explicitly supports `None` values for `tracer_provider` and `meter_provider` parameters (defaults to None). When None, OTEL SDK uses its built-in no-op providers.

## Testing

**Before:** Plugin crashes with `NotImplementedError`
**After:** Plugin starts successfully with telemetry disabled

## Changes

- Filter "none" from OTEL_TRACES_EXPORTER and OTEL_METRICS_EXPORTER env vars
- Return None from get_trace_provider/get_metric_provider when exporters list empty
- Bump version 0.0.41 → 0.0.42
- Update CHANGELOG.md

## Deployment

1. After merge, we need to rebuild platform-plugins images (auto-picks latest version)
2. Cut a new platform release

author: copilot
body:
Bot was systematically losing money: 60% of profit targets resulted in net losses after fees, and stop losses were tighter than net profit targets (inverted risk/reward).

## Core Issue

Coinbase fees: 1.4% round-trip. Profit targets at 0.8%, 1.0%, 1.2% = net losses of -0.6%, -0.4%, -0.2% respectively. Combined with -0.5% stops, this created negative mathematical expectancy requiring 83% win rate to break even.

## Changes

**Profit Targets** - All now net profitable after fees
- Coinbase: Updated from 0.8-2.0% to 1.6-5.0% (net +0.2% to +3.6%)
- Kraken: Updated from 0.5-3.0% to 1.0-4.0% (net +0.4% to +3.4%)

**Stop Losses** - Sized for 2:1 reward/risk ratio
- Coinbase: -0.5% → -1.25% (2:1 with 2.5% target)
- Kraken: -0.8% → -1.0% (2:1 with 2.0% target)

**Exit Behavior** - Allow positions to reach targets
- Disabled `COINBASE_EXIT_ANY_LOSS` (was exiting at -0.01%)
- Increased `COINBASE_MAX_HOLD_MINUTES` from 30 to 60

**Kraken Broker** - Fixed method signature
- Added `verbose: bool = True` parameter to `get_account_balance()` to match calling code

## Example

```python
# Before: Net loss after fees
target = 1.2  # 1.2% profit target
fees = 1.4    # 1.4% Coinbase round-trip
net = 1.2 - 1.4 = -0.2%  # ❌ Loss on winning trade

# After: Net profit after fees  
target = 2.5  # 2.5% profit target
fees = 1.4    # 1.4% Coinbase round-trip
net = 2.5 - 1.4 = +1.1%  # ✅ Profit on winning trade
```

## Impact

Breakeven win rate: 83% → 53%. Expected profitability with 55% win rate (achievable with existing 75/100 entry filter).

author: cmm25
body:
This pull request refactors how lesson and unit metadata are managed and displayed in the Swahili lessons feature. It moves lesson structure data (like titles, descriptions, categories, and emojis) into a centralized module (`lesson-structure`), updates the UI to use this richer metadata, and introduces XP-based level locking. The changes also streamline category handling and improve the logic for awarding XP and showing progress.

**Lesson and unit metadata improvements:**

* Replaces hardcoded lesson and unit data in `swahili/app/lessons/page.tsx` with imports from a new centralized `lesson-structure` module, enabling richer metadata (title, description, emoji, categories) for both lessons and units. ([swahili/app/lessons/page.tsxL6-R17](diffhunk://#diff-8588cc8218464d53740cf01b2e3f2a19e610b0c6d69185ff349111ab5ffa224aL6-R17), [swahili/app/lessons/[lessonId]/page.tsxL10-R24](diffhunk://#diff-a8e1bf530b60e3917747622444e6f982b14f4754e3150709cc65b18a640e4241L10-R24))
* Updates UI components to use `emoji` and `description` fields instead of category icons and subtitles, providing a more visually engaging and descriptive experience. ([swahili/app/lessons/[lessonId]/page.tsxL397-R408](diffhunk://#diff-a8e1bf530b60e3917747622444e6f982b14f4754e3150709cc65b18a640e4241L397-R408), [swahili/app/lessons/[lessonId]/page.tsxL407-R418](diffhunk://#diff-a8e1bf530b60e3917747622444e6f982b14f4754e3150709cc65b18a640e4241L407-R418), [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-8588cc8218464d53740cf01b2e3f2a19e610b0c6d69185ff349111ab5ffa224aL106-R104) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-8588cc8218464d53740cf01b2e3f2a19e610b0c6d69185ff349111ab5ffa224aL123-R118)

**Lesson loading and category handling:**

* Refactors lesson detail page logic to use the new `getLessonById` function for retrieving lesson definitions and resolving categories, improving maintainability and flexibility for future lesson additions. ([swahili/app/lessons/[lessonId]/page.tsxL205-R246](diffhunk://#diff-a8e1bf530b60e3917747622444e6f982b14f4754e3150709cc65b18a640e4241L205-R246), [swahili/app/lessons/[lessonId]/page.tsxR270-R281](diffhunk://#diff-a8e1bf530b60e3917747622444e6f982b14f4754e3150709cc65b18a640e4241R270-R281))
* Simplifies and improves category resolution when fetching vocabulary words, supporting category normalization and fallback behavior. ([swahili/app/lessons/[lessonId]/page.tsxL205-R246](diffhunk://#diff-a8e1bf530b60e3917747622444e6f982b14f4754e3150709cc65b18a640e4241L205-R246))

**XP and progress tracking:**

* Adds support for XP-based level locking: levels can now require a minimum XP to unlock, and the UI reflects locked/unlocked states accordingly.
* Ensures XP is only awarded once per lesson completion and integrates with the streak system for consistent XP tracking. ([swahili/app/lessons/[lessonId]/page.tsxR126-R134](diffhunk://#diff-a8e1bf530b60e3917747622444e6f982b14f4754e3150709cc65b18a640e4241R126-R134), [swahili/app/lessons/[lessonId]/page.tsxL304-R318](diffhunk://#diff-a8e1bf530b60e3917747622444e6f982b14f4754e3150709cc65b18a640e4241L304-R318))

**UI/UX improvements:**

* Improves loading state handling by showing a loading message while lesson data is being fetched, and streamlines the lesson detail page's conditional rendering. ([swahili/app/lessons/[lessonId]/page.tsxR341-R353](diffhunk://#diff-a8e1bf530b60e3917747622444e6f982b14f4754e3150709cc65b18a640e4241R341-R353), [swahili/app/lessons/[lessonId]/page.tsxL349-L361](diffhunk://#diff-a8e1bf530b60e3917747622444e6f982b14f4754e3150709cc65b18a640e4241L349-L361))
* Refines logic for displaying completion badges, current indicators, and progress bars to account for locked and unlocked states. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-8588cc8218464d53740cf01b2e3f2a19e610b0c6d69185ff349111ab5ffa224aL54-R78) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-8588cc8218464d53740cf01b2e3f2a19e610b0c6d69185ff349111ab5ffa224aL95-R87) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-8588cc8218464d53740cf01b2e3f2a19e610b0c6d69185ff349111ab5ffa224aL146-R138)

**Code cleanup:**

* Removes unused types and redundant code related to category handling, making the codebase cleaner and easier to maintain. ([swahili/app/lessons/[lessonId]/page.tsxL39-L42](diffhunk://#diff-a8e1bf530b60e3917747622444e6f982b14f4754e3150709cc65b18a640e4241L39-L42))

These changes collectively make the lesson experience more data-driven, visually appealing, and robust in handling lesson progression and user rewards.…ed lesson structure, enhancing maintainability and consistency. author: dingding229
body:
### Motivation
- Fix HDSKY duplicate detection when torrent title attributes are missing so existing seeds can be found from the search page links.
- Provide a standalone `DoubanMovieGenerator` implementation so `SSD` can reliably obtain fkgen data and avoid `TypeError` when older generators don't accept `douban_cookie` in the constructor.
- Improve cookie handling and upload/duplicate status reporting across several trackers to make uploads and duplicate detection more robust.

### Description
- Add `src/fkgen.py` implementing `DoubanMovieGenerator` which parses Douban pages and exposes `movie_info` and a safe `_cookie_dict` helper.
- Add `src/image777.py` compatibility shim exposing `upload_image` that returns `None` when no uploader is configured to keep image upload code paths safe.
- Improve `HDSKY` (`src/trackers/HDSKY.py`) by changing the search URL, adding `torrent_url`, adding a fallback loop to collect `details.php?id=` links when `title` attributes are missing, and update upload/duplicate handling to populate `meta["tracker_status"]` on duplicates and successful uploads more reliably.
- Small change to `CHDBITS` to introduce `torrent_url` constant and minor formatting cleanup in upload success logging.
- Add `torrent_url` constant to `OURBITS` and adjust its upload parsing to set `meta["tracker_status"]` on duplicate and success paths.
- Large SSD (`src/trackers/SSD.py`) improvements including using the new `DoubanMovieGenerator` without passing cookie at construction, setting `generator.douban_cookie` only when present, adding `_load_cookie_header` to normalize cookie files, making `search_existing` use a header-based request with loaded cookie string, tightening `curl` upload handling to return `True`/`False` and set richer `meta['tracker_status']` messages, and multiple robustness fixes around cookie checks and early returns.

### Testing
- No automated tests were executed for these changes.

author: bungcip
body:
This PR enhances the rule engine to support state transition checks by exposing `self` (new state) and `old` (previous state) in assertion expressions.

Changes:
- `crates/gurih_runtime/src/evaluator.rs`: Added support for dot notation in `Expression::Field` to traverse nested JSON objects.
- `crates/gurih_runtime/src/data.rs`: Updated `check_rules` to construct a context containing `self` and `old` alongside flattened fields.
- `crates/gurih_runtime/tests/rule_test.rs`: Added test case `test_rule_self_and_old` to verify `self.amount > old.amount` logic.

This allows defining rules like `assert "self.amount > old.amount"` to enforce invariants across updates.

body:
## Summary

Fixes a panic in `node:crypto` when using `createDecipheriv` with `setAutoPadding(false)` (denoland/deno#31957).

Two cases caused panics in `DecipherContext::final`:
1. **Empty input** — `GenericArray::from_slice` panicked on a 0-length slice when it expected 16 bytes. Now returns `Ok(())` early.
2. **Invalid block length** (not a multiple of 16 bytes) — the assertion inside `generic-array` panicked. Now uses the existing `assert_block_len!` macro to return `DecipherError::InvalidFinalBlockLength` instead.

Affected cipher modes: `Aes128Cbc`, `Aes128Ecb`, `Aes192Ecb`, `Aes256Ecb`, `Aes256Cbc`.

## Changes

- `ext/node/ops/crypto/cipher.rs` — added empty-input guard and `assert_block_len!` validation for all 5 affected `(cipher, auto_pad=false)` match arms
- `tests/unit_node/crypto/crypto_cipher_test.ts` — regression tests for both empty input and invalid block length scenarios

## Test plan

- [x] Unit tests for empty input with `setAutoPadding(false)` across all affected ciphers
- [x] Unit tests for invalid block length (10 bytes) returning `RangeError` instead of panicking
- [ ] `cargo test -p deno_node` passes

Fixes #31957

body:
Fixes two issues: waveform visualization fails to load on Windows due to file locking, and metronome stops ticking after first loop iteration.

## Changes

**Waveform loading (VideoMixer.load_audio)**
- Reordered waveform extraction to occur before `audio_track.load(p)` 
- Prevents Windows file lock from `pygame.mixer.music.load` blocking `pygame.mixer.Sound` access needed for waveform data

**Metronome loop sync (VideoProcessor.run)**
- Reset `metronome.current_beat = start_beats - 1.0` when loop restarts
- Ensures `check_tick()` comparison `int(beat_pos) > int(current_beat)` triggers on loop downbeat

```python
# Loop reset block now includes metronome state reset
if elapsed_ms >= loop_duration_ms:
    if self.mixer.audio_track.enabled:
        self.mixer.audio_track.play(int(loop_start_ms))
    with self.lock: 
        self.start_time = now
    total_beats = start_beats
    # Reset metronome to one beat before loop start so check_tick() detects the downbeat
    self.mixer.metronome.current_beat = start_beats - 1.0
```

> 1. **Waveform not loading:** The waveform visualization in the timeline widget never appears. This is likely due to `pygame.mixer.music.load` locking the file on Windows, preventing `pygame.mixer.Sound` (used for waveform extraction) from opening it subsequently.
> 2. **Metronome Sync:** The metronome stops ticking correctly after the first loop iteration. This happens because the metronome's internal state (`current_beat`) is not reset when the video processor loops back, causing the beat detection logic to fail for the first beat of the new loop.

>     *   Set `self.mixer.metronome.current_beat` to `start_beats - 1.0`. This ensures that when the beat position resets to `start_beats`, the metronome logic (`if cb > int(self.current_beat)`) correctly registers the downbeat.

### **Context**
This PR implements Node.js 24 support for all Azure CLI tasks (V1, V2, and V3)
[AB#2339106](https://dev.azure.com/mseng/b924d696-3eae-4116-8443-9a18392d8544/_workitems/edit/2339106)

---

- AzureCLIV1
- AzureCLIV2
- AzureCLIV3

---

### **Description**
This PR adds Node 24 runtime support to all three versions of the Azure CLI tasks

---

### **Risk Assessment** (Low / Medium / High) 
Medium

**Reasoning:**
- Node 24 runtime addition is additive and does not modify existing Node 20 execution handlers
- Dependencies are updated to versions that maintain backward compatibility
- No breaking changes to task behavior, inputs, or outputs, but not all cases might be covered
- Changes follow established patterns for multi-node runtime support in Azure Pipelines tasks

**Mitigating Factors:**
- Existing Node 20_1 handlers remain unchanged and operational
- Node 24 support is standard across Azure Pipelines task ecosystem
- Task library updates (`azure-pipelines-task-lib` v5) are designed for forward compatibility

---

This change cannot be behind a feature flag

---

### **Tech Design / Approach**
N

N

---

N

---

### **Additional Testing Performed**
**Build Validation:**
- ✅ Successfully built all three tasks with Node 24 configuration using `node make.js build`
- ✅ Verified generated artifacts in `_generated/AzureCLI{V1,V2,V3}_Node24/`
- ✅ Confirmed dependency resolution with Node 24-compatible package locks

**Dependency Audits:**
- ✅ Verified `azure-pipelines-task-lib` v5.2.4 compatibility with Node 24
- ✅ Confirmed `azure-devops-node-api` v15.1.3 supports Node 24

N

N

### **Rollback Scenario and Process** (Yes/No)
**Rollback Strategy:**
1. **Agent-Level Mitigation**: If Node 24 runtime issues are discovered, agents can be configured to prefer Node 20 handlers
2. **Task Version Pinning**: Users experiencing issues can pin to previous task versions (V1: 1.269.0, V2: 2.269.0, V3: 3.268.1) that only support Node 20
3. **Task override**: Task can be overridden with the documented TSG
4. **Code Rollback**: Revert this PR and remove Node 24 handlers from task manifests
5. **Dependency Rollback**: If library incompatibilities arise, revert dependency updates while retaining Node 20 support

N

author: asim
body:
## Summary

`micro run` now provides a complete development experience by starting an HTTP gateway alongside your services.

## The New Experience

```bash
$ micro new helloworld
$ cd helloworld
$ micro run
```

```
  ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
  │                                                             │
  │   Micro                                                     │
  │                                                             │
  │   Web:     http://localhost:8080                            │
  │   API:     http://localhost:8080/api/{service}/{method}     │
  │   Health:  http://localhost:8080/health                     │
  │                                                             │
  │   Services:                                                 │
  │     ● helloworld                                            │
  │                                                             │
  │   Watching for changes...                                   │
  │                                                             │
  └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

Open http://localhost:8080 to see your services and call them from the browser.

## Features

| URL | Description |
|-----|-------------|
| `/` | Web dashboard - browse and call services |
| `/api/{service}/{method}` | API gateway - HTTP to RPC proxy |
| `/health` | Health checks - aggregated service health |
| `/services` | Service list - JSON |

## New Flags

```bash
micro run                    # Gateway on :8080 (default)
micro run --address :3000    # Custom gateway port
micro run --no-gateway       # Services only, no HTTP gateway
```

## Philosophy

> "When you have something that's intuitive, almost like a consumer product, you don't need anyone to explain it to you. It just works."

The gateway is now part of the core experience. No separate processes, no extra setup. `micro run` gives you everything you need.

## Files

- `cmd/micro/run/gateway/gateway.go` - HTTP gateway implementation
- `cmd/micro/run/run.go` - Integration and startup banner
- Updated README.md and docs

author: mcodex
body:
This pull request introduces major improvements to monster detection, targeting consistency, and attack management for the cavebot and targetbot systems. The main changes include integrating a new AttackStateMachine as the centralized attack handler, enhancing monster detection logic to prevent leaving monsters behind, and refining the smart pull and dynamic lure behaviors for smoother and more responsive bot operation.

**Monster Detection & Targeting Enhancements:**

* Increased monster detection and targeting ranges (`MONSTER_DETECTION_RANGE` and `MONSTER_TARGETING_RANGE`) for better coverage and to prevent the bot from missing monsters when moving between waypoints. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-6f084b23e7807f2f537e98cc8ce633a4e6d448903b0fa1fa42bc18ad799b0607R7-R14) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-6f084b23e7807f2f537e98cc8ce633a4e6d448903b0fa1fa42bc18ad799b0607L1830-R1907) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-6f084b23e7807f2f537e98cc8ce633a4e6d448903b0fa1fa42bc18ad799b0607L2032-R2110)
* Introduced `TargetBot.hasTargetableMonstersOnScreen` and `TargetBot.shouldWaitForMonsters` to reliably determine when cavebot movement should pause due to nearby monsters. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-6f084b23e7807f2f537e98cc8ce633a4e6d448903b0fa1fa42bc18ad799b0607R1193-R1253) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-b6d86af6cdcfdec6c6d850690a305d5395c7a5cc98d936b69fdd4513457a48dbL966-R977)
* Improved monster detection logic in `cavebot.lua` to check for targetable monsters before proceeding to the next waypoint, ensuring no monsters are left behind.

**Attack State Machine Integration:**

* Integrated `AttackStateMachine` as the primary attack handler, providing linear, consistent targeting and eliminating competing attack sources. All attack requests now go through this state machine for unified management. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-6f084b23e7807f2f537e98cc8ce633a4e6d448903b0fa1fa42bc18ad799b0607R25-R31) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-c11b93d53a67867ceffa0eb330a7da51bb8ecc35eaf98ef2d0e10e28fc36384cR78-R80) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-1886534f83d77de7008f7d8d0060fc8bd5c8133f3402a4e8c18fcd7591f801a6R893-R912) [[4]](diffhunk://#diff-6f084b23e7807f2f537e98cc8ce633a4e6d448903b0fa1fa42bc18ad799b0607R89-L138)
* Updated `TargetBot.requestAttack` to use the new state machine, including improved dead checks and priority calculations for targets.

**Smart Pull & Dynamic Lure Improvements:**

* Enhanced smart pull logic with streak-based activation/deactivation and improved threat detection, resulting in smoother waypoint pausing and resuming. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-619b338d5005e1105ccfe7dc0bc282c5d113596f0be7c36811e40897754ee332R18-R19) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-619b338d5005e1105ccfe7dc0bc282c5d113596f0be7c36811e40897754ee332R1422-R1497)
* Improved dynamic lure logic to trigger more responsively and only when appropriate, reducing unnecessary pauses.

**Target Prioritization:**

* Refined target prioritization by factoring in distance, health, and MonsterAI adjustments, leading to smarter target selection. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-6f084b23e7807f2f537e98cc8ce633a4e6d448903b0fa1fa42bc18ad799b0607R1850-R1867) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-6f084b23e7807f2f537e98cc8ce633a4e6d448903b0fa1fa42bc18ad799b0607R1935) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-6f084b23e7807f2f537e98cc8ce633a4e6d448903b0fa1fa42bc18ad799b0607R1957) [[4]](diffhunk://#diff-6f084b23e7807f2f537e98cc8ce633a4e6d448903b0fa1fa42bc18ad799b0607R1990)

**Performance & Responsiveness:**

* Reduced attack command intervals for faster, more responsive attacking.
* Lowered recalc cooldown for target selection, and ensured regular updates to the attack state machine.

These changes collectively make the bot more reliable in combat, prevent it from missing monsters, and ensure attack commands are consistent and efficient.

author: gsantiago-orbis
body:
### TL;DR

Improved container testing infrastructure with Docker/Podman flexibility and optimized Docker build process.

### What changed?

- Added support for configurable container runtime by introducing `CONTAINER_RUNTIME` environment variable (defaults to "docker")
- Fixed case sensitivity issue by renaming `Internal-bgp.js` imports to `internal-bgp.js`
- Optimized Docker build by adding `--ignore-scripts --omit=dev` flags to `bun install` in Dockerfile
- Updated development script from `tsx watch` to `bun run --watch` in package.json
- Enhanced container tests with better error handling and logging
- Fixed authentication in container tests by adding proper auth context to RPC calls
- Improved code formatting and readability in test files

### How to test?

1. Run container tests with Docker (default):
   ```
   bun test
   ```

2. Run container tests with Podman:
   ```
   CONTAINER_RUNTIME=podman bun test
   ```

3. Verify that the orchestrator builds and runs correctly with the optimized Dockerfile:
   ```
   docker build -f packages/orchestrator/Dockerfile -t catalyst-node:test .
   docker run -p 3000:3000 catalyst-node:test
   ```

### Why make this change?

This change improves development and testing flexibility by allowing developers to use either Docker or Podman as their container runtime. It also optimizes the Docker build process by skipping unnecessary scripts and development dependencies, resulting in faster builds and smaller images. The case sensitivity fix for the BGP module ensures consistent behavior across different file systems and platforms.

 12: assign stack(3) = stack(5)
 15: line 14:   print("These are the incorrect booleans")
 17: call-utility stack(7) = print(const("These are the incorrect booleans"))
 23: assign stack(7) = null
 25: line 15:   print(res_v == true)
 27: validated operator stack(6) = stack(3) == const(true)
 32: call-utility stack(7) = print(stack(6))
```

In `2` a function state object gets assigned to `stack(6)`. Later in `27` without any additional setup on `stack(6)`, it is used as target for a validated operator call between two booleans. 

Validated operator calls assume the type of the destination variant to be correct so they only set the variant data. The type stays `OBJECT` because formerly a function state was stored inside. In addition setting the data to this boolean only corrupts the variants `ObjectID`, the raw pointer stays untouched so the variant is still somewhat usable as object.

The issue happens, because `stack(6)` is a temporary which was added with a `bool` type. `get_bool` is only a coroutine in an inherited class, but the method in the base class is not a coroutine. The compiler uses the typehint from the baseclass to create the temporary, which results in a `bool` temporary.

This PR changes the compiler to always use an untyped temporary for the result of an awaited call, because we can't check whether an inherited class might have turned the sync function into a coroutine.

Another option would be to let the analyzer mark all types of expressions after an `await` with `is_coroutine`. But the compiler solution seemed less invasive to me.

author: garvit-joshi
body:
## Summary

- Add `@RateLimit` annotation for controlling request throughput across distributed systems
- Use Redisson's `RRateLimiter` for distributed rate limiting
- Support both annotation-based and programmatic (`LocksmithRateLimitTemplate`) approaches
- Include optional Micrometer metrics integration

## Features

- **@RateLimit annotation** with configurable:
  - `permits` - number of permits per interval (default: 10)
  - `interval` - time interval (default: "1s")
  - `type` - OVERALL (shared) or PER_CLIENT rate limiting
  - `mode` - SKIP_IMMEDIATELY or WAIT_AND_SKIP
  - `skipHandler` - custom handling when rate limit exceeded

- **LocksmithRateLimitTemplate** for programmatic usage with fluent builder API

- **RateLimitMetrics** for Micrometer integration (enabled via `locksmith.rate-limit.metrics-enabled=true`)

## Usage

```java
// Basic: 10 requests per second (defaults)
@RateLimit(key = "api-call")
public void apiCall() { }

// Custom rate: 100 requests per minute
@RateLimit(key = "heavy-operation", permits = 100, interval = "1m")
public void heavyOperation() { }

// Per-user rate limiting with SpEL
@RateLimit(key = "#{#userId}", permits = 5, interval = "1s")
public void userAction(String userId) { }
```

## Test plan

- [x] Unit tests for RateLimitAspect
- [x] Unit tests for RateLimitMetrics
- [x] Unit tests for skip handlers
- [x] Unit tests for LocksmithRateLimitTemplate
- [x] Integration tests with Testcontainers Redis

Closes #7

author: glastonbridge
body:
As a proposed approach, I have replaced the current "save" buttons with "share" as this is the intuitive action on mobile. I have also put in some different text for sharing, but kept the flow otherwise roughly the same.

### Android

[Screen_recording_20260127_153909.webm](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/1d1dfebb-ac43-4f4d-9181-7543466f99b0)

### iOS

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/cc616a4e-057b-418b-8485-92723caee4ec


The current "Save" button in the app has two roles: (1) as the individual user's project storage and (2) as a project exporter. Knowing that multiple project support is coming, I expect the usage of this button will be more likely just a project export function, and Sharesheets are intended for this use. If we do need filesystem-like access, the Sharesheets provide that functionality as an option.

## Details

* We don't display a "sharing complete" toast as the behaviour is more obvious in the mobile sharing flow and it seems overly verbose to show the user.
* The text on the "share" version of the save dialogs is different to reflect the changes in the user's expectations and next steps, but it's just a first proposal.
* There are several places where I have not updated the "Save" flow to become the "Share" flow because they seem to fit the "individual project storage" role above. I'm very open to being wrong about this!
  * The NameProjectDialog has a save button
  * OpenSharedProjectPage offers a save to avoid overwriting the user's currently-active project
  * ImportPage offers a save to avoid overwriting the user's currently-active project

author: voodoohop
body:
## Problem

The deploy-enter-services workflow failed because the server had divergent branches:

```
err: hint: You have divergent branches and need to specify how to reconcile them.
```

This happened because someone had checked out a different branch on the server (`fix/register-endpoint-auth-bypass`) and the local `production` branch was 20 commits behind the remote.

## Solution

Replace `git pull origin <branch>` with:
```bash
git fetch origin <branch>
git checkout <branch> 2>/dev/null || git checkout -b <branch> origin/<branch>
git reset --hard origin/<branch>
```

This ensures:
1. The server always matches the remote branch exactly
2. Works regardless of what branch was previously checked out
3. Handles divergent branches by force-resetting to remote state

## Changes

- Updated both staging and production deployment scripts in `deploy-enter-services.yml`

## Testing

Manually fixed the server by running the same commands via SSH - deployment now works correctly.

author: gary-van-woerkens
body:
Add exception handler to catch duplicate_table error when creating partitions.

In high-concurrency scenarios (importDate.ts uses pAll with concurrency: 10), multiple concurrent calls to insert_into_matomo_partitioned can attempt to create the same partition simultaneously. The IF NOT EXISTS check doesn't prevent this race condition - between the check and the CREATE TABLE execution, another process can create the partition.

This results in "relation already exists" errors that crash the import process.

Solution: Add EXCEPTION handler to catch duplicate_table errors and silently ignore them, as this is an expected situation in concurrent environments.

author: ajassani
body:
Previously, get_kernel_launchers used fixed-depth traversal (child->grandchild) to find kernels, which failed when python functions were added to the tree since they became intermediate nodes between cpu_op and runtime events.

This change rewrites the method to work backwards from kernels:
1. Find each kernel's runtime parent
2. Walk up from runtime, skipping python_function nodes
3. Use first cpu_op found as launcher, or runtime event if none found

Benefits:
- Consistent results regardless of add_python_func setting
- Simplified to single pass (was two passes)
- Removed ~35 lines of code

Also adds 19 unit tests covering edge cases:
- Python function skipping
- Unlinked runtime events (no cpu_op parent)
- NCCL kernel handling
- Graph launch (cudaGraphLaunch/hipGraphLaunch)
- Nested cpu_ops and execute pattern
- Memory operations (memcpy/memset)

author: aleph-prover-test[bot]
body:
Proven lemmas: 1/1

The goal is to prove that if real numbers a and b satisfy the linear system 3·a + 2·b = 5 and a + b = 2, then necessarily a = 1 and b = 1 (i.e., the unique solution is (1,1)). The proof is decomposed into two sub-goals: first derive ha : a = 1 from the two given equations, and then derive hb : b = 1 from the same equations. Both sub-goals have been solved: Lean uses the linarith tactic to eliminate variables and conclude each equality directly from h₀ and h₁. With ha and hb established, the final step bundles them into the conjunction a = 1 ∧ b = 1. So progress is complete: 2 out of 2 key sub-results are proven, and nothing remains. An interesting aspect is that while the system can be solved manually by simple elimination (e.g., subtracting 2·(a+b)=4 from 3a+2b=5 to get a=1), linarith automates this linear reasoning cleanly.

# Implementierung der Backup-Funktionalität für blaues H5P

## Zusammenfassung
Diese PR implementiert die Backup- und Restore-Funktionalität für blaue H5P-Aktivitäten (`h5pactivity`), indem der Kursfortschritt persistent im Gradebook gespeichert wird. Dies stellt sicher, dass der Fortschritt bei Backup/Restore-Operationen erhalten bleibt.

## Problem
Der Fortschritt von blauen H5P-Aktivitäten wurde nur in User Preferences gespeichert und ging bei Kurs-Backup/Restore verloren.

## Lösung
- **Neue Funktion:** `setgrade_h5pactivity()` speichert Scores direkt im Gradebook
- **3-stufige Priorität:** Cache → Gradebook → Completion State
- **Automatische Integration:** Fortschritt wird bei jeder Interaktion im Gradebook gespeichert

## Geänderte Dateien
- `classes/local/utils.php` (+116, -6): Neue Gradebook-Integration und erweiterte Fortschrittslogik
- `externallib.php` (+4): Integration des Gradebook-Aufrufs
- `version.php` (2026012516): Version erhöht

## Testing
- [ ] Blauen H5P-Aktivitäten lösen
- [ ] Blauen H5P-Aktivitäten löschen
- [ ] Kurs wiederherstellen
- [ ] Fortschritt im wiederhergestellten Kurs überprüfen

## Description
This PR significantly strengthens the test suite for `r.geomorphon` by adding **_reference-data based validation_** using the NC dataset (nc_spm_full_v2beta1).

Tests now validate algorithm behavior by **comparing outputs against reference data**, improving regression detection and ensuring stability across parameters, flags, and modes.
Earlier smoke-style checks (mean, stddev bounds and consistency checks) have been replaced with reference comparisons.

## Changes
- Algorithm validation using referenced univariate statistics for real and synthetic data
- Parameter validation for search/skip constraints, flatness threshold, and required outputs
- Reference-based validation of multiple outputs (`forms`, `ternary`, `intensity`, `elongation`)
- Flag behavior validation for extended correction (`-e`) and meter units (`-m`)
- Reference validation of comparison modes (`anglev1`, `anglev2`, `anglev2_distance`)
- JSON profile output format validation

## Test Results
Test coverage increased from 2 to 12.
All tests pass successfully.


Notes: 

- The latest commit validates r.geomorphon outputs against fixed reference data from the NC (nc_spm_full_v2beta1) dataset. Earlier commits only used lightweight sanity checks such as mean/stddev bounds and consistency checks. 
- Some slow tests are skipped for CI

### **User description** ## Description Fixes #93 The IsFile() function in pkg/typing/types.go uses `panic()` to handle file close errors. This can crash the application when running on network filesystems or container volumes where I/O errors may occur during `file.Close()`. For read-only file handles, close errors can be safely ignored. This PR removes the panic and silently discards the close error. **Before:** ```go defer func() { if err == nil && file != nil { deferErr := file.Close() if deferErr != nil { panic(deferErr) } } }() ``` After : ```go defer func() { if file != nil { _ = file.Close() } }() ``` ___ ### **PR Type** Bug fix ___ ### **Description** - Remove panic on file close error in IsFile() function - Safely ignore close errors for read-only file handles - Prevent application crashes on network filesystems ___ ### Diagram Walkthrough ```mermaid flowchart LR A["IsFile() function"] --> B["Open file"] B --> C["Defer cleanup"] C --> D["Old: panic on close error"] C --> E["New: silently ignore close error"] D --> F["Application crash risk"] E --> G["Graceful error handling"] ```

author: fritzprix
body:
SENTINEL SECURITY PATCH: Memory Safety Vulnerability (Critical)

🧨 **Threat:** Potential double-free / memory corruption due to `unsafe` pointer casting.
In `src-tauri/src/lib.rs`, an `unsafe` block was used to convert a static reference (`&'static MCPServiceProxyManager`) into an `Arc<MCPServiceProxyManager>` by casting the reference to a raw pointer and using `Arc::from_raw`. The resulting `Arc` was then cloned, and the original `Arc` was "forgotten" using `std::mem::forget`. This pattern relies on assumptions about the internal layout of `Arc` and the allocator that may not hold for static data, and creates a "fake" Arc that believes it owns memory it does not. When the cloned Arc is dropped, it attempts to decrement the reference count of the unmanaged memory, leading to potential undefined behavior or allocator corruption.

🛡️ **Defense:** Refactored Global State Management.
Instead of trying to fake shared ownership, the `MCPServiceProxyManager` is now properly wrapped in an `Arc` *before* being stored in the global `OnceLock` in `src-tauri/src/state.rs`. The global getter `get_mcp_service_proxy_manager()` now returns a cloned `Arc`, which safely shares ownership of the underlying manager instance. The `unsafe` block in `lib.rs` has been completely removed.

**CVSS Estimate:** High (Memory Corruption potential in core component)

author: lo48576
body:
# Issue

If the preedit was confirmed by a `commit-unhandled` command, the preedit buffer is not properly updated (at least visually).

```
$ echo 'A RET' | ./tools/skk
{ "input": "A RET", "output": "あ", "preedit": "▽あ" }
$
```

In this example, RET (or `C-m`, both are `commit-unhandled` by default) commits `あ`, so the `あ` in the preedit is expected to be cleared.

This issue makes https://github.com/fcitx/fcitx5-skk/pull/24 hard to fix, since the downstream applications cannot know the actual preedit content through libskk API.

# Fix
Tries to build the string representation of the preedit anyway, to check whether preedit was actually changed or not.
This may be inefficient, but straight-forward and at least not incorrect.

The root cause of the issue is the ambiguity of the return value of `process_key_event`: it represents both of "whether the key event is consumed by libskk" and "whether the key event may change libskk context and state", while they are not always equal.

The elegant way to fix this would be to separate them into two booleans, but I'm not confident this can be achieved without breaking API changes, so I went straight-forward way this time.
Adding private fields (such as `bool preedit_is_changed;`) to `State` and referring it from `Context` may also be possible, but it would make the logic complex and error-prone, so I'd like to avoid this and prefer the extra string manipulation by `update_preedit()`.

Implement a new Defect Management Agent module that provides an intelligent, conversation-based defect submission and tracking system. This feature enables users to submit defects using natural language, with AI-powered validation and structured data extraction.

## Key Changes

### Documentation & Design
- Added comprehensive design document (`doc/20.defect-agent.md`) covering:
  - Defect lifecycle and state machine (draft → reviewing → submitted → assigned → processing → resolved → closed)
  - Data models for templates, reports, and messages
  - Complete API specification (templates, defects, messages, attachments)
  - AI review logic and system prompts
  - Frontend component architecture
  
- Added product specification (`doc/21.defect-agent-product.md`) with:
  - User scenarios and core value propositions
  - Severity and priority levels
  - Template system design
  - AI polish and message collaboration features
  
- Added reusable patterns document (`doc/21.reusable-patterns.md`) documenting:
  - Soft delete with recycle bin pattern
  - Folder-based classification system
  - Space isolation for future multi-tenant support

### Frontend Implementation
- Created `DefectAgentPage` with tab-based filtering (assigned/submitted/completed/rejected)
- Implemented `DefectList` component with table view and status badges
- Built `DefectSubmitPanel` for conversation-style defect submission
- Added `DefectDetailPanel` for viewing and managing individual defects
- Created `TemplateDialog` for template management
- Added utility functions (`defectContentUtils.ts`) for parsing `[IMG]` tags in content
- Integrated with existing design system (GlassCard, TabBar, Button components)
- Added route registration in `App.tsx` with permission checks

### Backend Models & Services
- Defined MongoDB collections:
  - `defect_templates`: Template configuration with required fields and AI prompts
  - `defect_reports`: Main defect records with structured data and status tracking
  - `defect_messages`: Conversation messages for AI review and collaboration
  
- Implemented state machine with 9 states supporting complete defect lifecycle
- Added support for attachments with COS storage integration
- Included version history tracking for defect modifications

### UI/UX Enhancements
- Updated `UsersPage` to visually distinguish bot users with green accent styling
- Fixed z-index layering in `AppShell` for proper modal stacking
- Added `@radix-ui/react-popover` dependency for enhanced UI components

### Data & Configuration

### State Machine
Implements standard ticket workflow with clear role-based transitions:
- Reporters: submit, supplement info, confirm resolution
- Assignees: accept, process, resolve, reject
- Admins: assign, manage templates, close tickets

## Testing Notes

All 25 unit tests for `DefectAgentController` pass, covering:
- Template CRUD operations
- Defect lifecycle transitions
- Message handling and AI review
- Permission validation
- Attachment management

🚨 Severity: HIGH
💡 Vulnerability: External scripts loaded from CDNs (Vega, WebR) lacked Subresource Integrity (SRI) hashes, allowing potential execution of malicious code if CDNs are compromised.

author: odaeus
body:
My colleague discovered that many of our tests were failing on a fresh build of a project due to an exception being raised when the Quantum package attempted to use the Logger:
```
Reason: shutdown: failed to start child: Integrations.Scheduler
  ** (EXIT) shutdown: failed to start child: Quantum. JobBroadcaster
    ** (EXIT) an exception was raised:
      ** (Protocol.UndefinedError) protocol String.Chars not implemented for type Tuple. This protocol is implemented for the following type(s): Atom, BitString, Date, DateTime, Decimal, Float, Integer, Lis

Got value:

    {"Loading Initial Jobs from Config", [node: :nonode@nohost]}

      (elixir 1.18.4) lib/string/chars.ex:3: String.Chars. impl_for!/1
      (elixir 1.18.4) lib/string/chars.ex:22: String. Chars.to_string/1
      (logger 1.18.4) lib/logger.ex:982: Logger.__do_10g__/4
      (quantum 3.5.3) lib/quantum/job_broadcaster.ex:51: Quantum.JobBroadcaster.init/1
```
We had recently upgraded to Elixir 1.18.4 and adjusted the logging config in our test environment to:
```
config :logger, always_evaluate_messages: true
```

We traced this down to Quantum's usage of giving anonymous functions that return a tuple to Logger calls. This is an officially supported case but the code path for forced evaluation was running the function and sending the entire result tuple as data to the Logger, which is no longer supported.

I've attempted to fix this by adjusting the forced evaluation functions to handle this case. Importantly, without accidentally adding in support for passing a tuple directly.

Please let me know if this does the job!

-- Andrew

author: brej-29
body:
This PR hardens and streamlines the local development experience and prepares for frictionless free deployment. It adds a richer Makefile, plus two new context docs to guide developers through local runs and free deployments.

What’s changed
- Makefile hardening and new workflow targets
  - Introduced cross-platform Docker Compose invocation via COMPOSE, defaulting to docker compose
  - Added targets: up, down, logs, migrate, seed, train-content, train-mf, run
  - Added a user-friendly help target that prints available make targets and their purpose
  - Added an alias alembic-upgrade: migrate for backward compatibility
  - Made the run target respect PORT, defaulting to 8000, and run uvicorn accordingly
  - Kept existing targets (e.g., test) intact
- New context docs (two new files)
  - context/RUN_LOCAL.md: Very detailed, step-by-step local run guide for Windows PowerShell and macOS/Linux bash, covering prerequisites, venv setup, dependency installation, env files, docker-compose startup, migrations, seeding, training, running the API, smoke tests, and lint/format/test steps
  - context/DEPLOY_FREE.md: Detailed guide for free deployment on Hugging Face Docker Spaces with Supabase Postgres and Upstash Redis, including architecture recap, how to configure DATABASE_URL and REDIS_URL, space settings, ephemeral storage considerations, startup/training on boot, verification steps, and troubleshooting
- Documentation and workflow integration
  - README will reference the new context docs to guide users toward local run and free deployment workflows
- Repo polish alignment with defaults
  - The new targets and help system align with a consistent local dev experience across Windows/macOS/Linux, using docker-compose for local Postgres/Redis and the existing app/run flow

How this solves the issue
- Reduces friction for local development by providing a single, cross-platform Makefile-driven workflow for common tasks (start services, migrations, seeding, training, and running the API).
- Provides explicit, in-repo guidance for running locally and for free deployment, making it easier for new contributors to get started and for teams to standardize on best practices.
- Keeps secrets and sensitive configs out of code; recommends env vars in .env and separate deployment configs for HF Spaces.

How to use (quick-start)
- Local dev (quick bootstrap):
  - make up           # start Postgres and Redis
  - make migrate      # run migrations
  - make seed         # seed the database
  - make train-content # train content-based model
  - make train-mf      # train matrix factorization model
  - make run           # run the FastAPI app (uvicorn)
- Optional quality checks:
  - make test          # run pytest
  - make lint          # run ruff lint checks
  - make fmt           # format code with Ruff

Notes for Windows users
- The COMPOSE variable uses docker compose; ensure Docker Desktop is configured (WSL2 backend). If you’re using legacy docker-compose, you can override COMPOSE accordingly (e.g., using docker-compose).

Next steps
- If you’d like, we can add helper scripts (scripts/run_local.ps1 and scripts/run_local.sh) to encapsulate the full local bootstrap flow.
- Consider adding optional auto-training-on-boot behavior to handle ephemeral HF Spaces storage in DEPLOY_FREE.md (as described in the docs).

Validation
- Ensure make up starts Postgres and Redis, make migrate applies migrations, make seed populates the DB, and make run starts the API on port 7860 by default (or the port configured via PORT).
- Follow the RUN_LOCAL.md and DEPLOY_FREE.md steps to reproduce the recommended workflows.

## Summary
This PR adds rich text editing capabilities to card templates by integrating Tiptap, a headless Vue/React rich text editor. It replaces the markdown-based approach with a full WYSIWYG editor that supports text formatting, lists, and structured content within multiline card slots.

## Key Changes

- **Added Tiptap dependencies**: Integrated `@tiptap/react`, `@tiptap/starter-kit`, and formatting extensions (color, text-align, underline) for rich text editing
- **Removed markdown dependency**: Replaced `marked` with `markdown-it` and Tiptap for better content handling
- **Updated template documentation**: Added `data-slot-multiline` attribute documentation and template design guidelines emphasizing consolidated content slots over fragmented ones
- **Refactored card templates**:
  - **daggerheart.html**: Restructured layout with absolute positioning, consolidated description and abilities into single rich content slot, updated styling to use CSS variables
  - **spell-scroll.html**: Adjusted dimensions to standard 63mm × 88mm, repositioned elements with absolute positioning, enhanced description formatting with rich text support
  - **rpg-card.html**: Updated `data-slot-type="html"` to `data-slot-multiline` for consistency
- **Added floating UI support**: Included `@floating-ui/dom` and related packages for positioning rich text menus

## Implementation Details

- Rich content slots now use `data-slot-multiline` attribute instead of `data-slot-type="html"`
- Templates leverage Tiptap's starter kit which includes essential formatting: bold, italic, strikethrough, headings, lists, code blocks, and blockquotes
- Card layouts now use absolute positioning with millimeter-based measurements for consistent printing
- Template design guidelines encourage consolidating related content (flavor text, abilities, effects) into single rich content areas rather than fragmenting into multiple slots, providing users more flexibility with formatting

body:
This pull request introduces a formal proof scaffold for the Agda kernel, adds basic property-based tests for novelty and fixed points, and integrates Agda proof checking into CI. It also improves documentation and policy around proof tooling, and implements a new host-side operation in the Python VM. The most important changes are grouped below.

**Agda formalization and proofs:**

* Added initial Agda proof scaffolds and basic lemmas for boundaries, fixed points, gauge invariants, minimal finiteness, novelty monotonicity, signature arities, and univalence, replacing postulates with minimal constructive definitions and proofs (`agda/Prism/Boundaries.agda`, `agda/Prism/FixedPoint.agda`, `agda/Prism/Gauge.agda`, `agda/Prism/MinPrism.agda`, `agda/Prism/Novelty.agda`, `agda/Prism/Signature.agda`, `agda/Prism/Univalence.agda`) [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-4dbf39c485e639c51098c9beafb8c09dfa32447be1897f0714513c08f09809c6L3-R15) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-b753fce3c5c83188e08cb18d539cc79a6c86a0adea0e8a0b98afe0720dbc5b4cL3-R15) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-f1f88da3f28aea1f41b375d7816df7a42fadaff6be6190a7725b4bb76ed0c622L3-R20) [[4]](diffhunk://#diff-91bccd5404b6785d942ca0064ed14af7e87125c69d60c7db2ebcd489909fa67eR3-R20) [[5]](diffhunk://#diff-f49dbdd9c0590ea930c548a6aa07c3f4c4498f1b43732035e30f3a99a3186301R3-R20) [[6]](diffhunk://#diff-bdd151c55f7d4fb7f05a4e835dab82e1e53564409066338fc96a5ab18eb6e790R4) [[7]](diffhunk://#diff-bdd151c55f7d4fb7f05a4e835dab82e1e53564409066338fc96a5ab18eb6e790R19-R40) [[8]](diffhunk://#diff-63316ec1023bb1890027ab56cd7dd73fcb33272eadeb7fe1c9e496fe9e8a0c5aR3-R12).
* Updated Agda README with local setup instructions and clarified the status as "scaffold + basic lemmas" (`agda/README.md`).

**CI/CD and proof tooling integration:**

* Added Agda proof checking to CI: new `agda-check` job in GitHub Actions, runs on `.agda` changes, and is required for report collection (`.github/workflows/ci-milestones.yml`) [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-2c2699d70e2e8913404a12cc52c6709985417b8cf73c5040c4db29a0f6e380dcR12) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-2c2699d70e2e8913404a12cc52c6709985417b8cf73c5040c4db29a0f6e380dcR119-R132) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-2c2699d70e2e8913404a12cc52c6709985417b8cf73c5040c4db29a0f6e380dcL314-R329).
* Added scripts for installing and checking Agda (`scripts/install_agda.sh`, `scripts/check_agda.sh`) [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-d9a680a7951075342f0d2a8a4f9dd1877f2e7e9722dba96466ef96db2bdf98b9R1-R22) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-475cb615cf6aa554fa66535e1afdcf66ef0d6b656fd5dfcb47e0b902728660f2R1-R18).
* Pinned Haskell and cabal toolchains in `mise.toml` for reproducible Agda builds.
* Updated policy to require Agda proof checks on GitHub-hosted runners and restrict toolchain installation on self-hosted runners (`POLICY_SEED.md`).

**Testing and property-based tests:**

* Added property-based tests for novelty monotonicity and fixed-point stabilization in the Python VM (`tests/min_prism/test_novelty_monotone.py`, `tests/min_prism/test_fixed_point_bounded.py`, `tests/min_prism/harness.py`) [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-fdc75d8bbd298b0cbf33da2ce212fa4e349afc43c8db958433201ceac2c38f23R1-R69) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-62b1ac15feef9942e4b4fab8fa660742a3021dad7441b1d54615d419b1329708R1-R53) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-cccc0259f46bf9933a9e8f4a7f6008c7591a7be709d5a3ea8f2004b943600042R50-R80).

**Python VM improvements:**

* Implemented `cd_lift_binary`, a host-only operation for componentwise binary ops on coordinate pairs (`prism_vm.py`).

**Documentation and milestone tracking:**

* Marked several formalization and proof milestones as complete in `IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md` and `MILESTONES.md` [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-aec82e4a332ae9d9131798e605a0fb50ec6bf6a4051e4706f5d64b2fc5f4151aL877-R881) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-39b04a90fa3cfbca2a128e889c2518cc7b1bfc8d08535c348d4f5955826d6a90L32-R36).

These changes collectively advance the formalization track, improve CI reliability for proofs, and add foundational property tests for the VM.

body:
## Summary

This PR improves error messages when an API provider (such as OpenAI-compatible proxies like kie.ai) does not properly support native function/tool calling.

## Problem

When using OpenAI-compatible proxies that do not fully support the function calling API, the model may output XML-formatted tool calls in its text response. The previous error messages were confusing for users:

- "XML tool calls are no longer supported. Remove any XML tool markup..."
- "Invalid tool call: missing tool_use.id. XML tool calls are no longer supported..."

These messages were technical and implied user error when the actual issue is API provider compatibility.

## Solution

Updated error messages to be more user-friendly:

1. **XML tool markup detection**: "The model is outputting XML-formatted tool calls instead of using native function calling. This typically happens when your API provider does not fully support OpenAI's function/tool calling feature. Please verify that your API provider supports native tool calling, or try using a different provider."

2. **Missing tool call ID**: "Invalid tool call: the model's tool call is missing a required ID. This typically happens when your API provider does not fully support OpenAI's function/tool calling feature. Please verify that your API provider supports native tool calling, or try using a different provider."

## Changes

- Updated `presentAssistantMessage.ts` with improved error messages
- Updated `BaseTool.ts` with consistent messaging
- Updated corresponding test files

## Testing

- All 15 affected tests pass
- Type checking passes
- Lint passes

Fixes #11011

`make book` fails when any of its component targets (tests, docs, or marimushka) are unavailable or fail, blocking documentation generation. Reported in projects without test infrastructure or with failing test suites, docs generation issues, or missing notebooks.

## Changes

- **Remove hard dependencies**: `book` target no longer depends on `test`, `docs`, or `marimushka` targets
- **Add conditional execution**: All three targets run opportunistically via `$(MAKE) <target> || printf warning`
- **Preserve existing behavior**: Component outputs (API docs, coverage, reports, notebooks) still included when available; missing sections already skip gracefully

```diff
-book:: test docs marimushka
+book:: install-uv
 	@printf "${BLUE}[INFO] Building combined documentation...${RESET}\n"
+	
+	# Run docs but don't fail book if docs fail or are unavailable
+	@$(MAKE) docs || printf "${YELLOW}[WARN] Docs failed or unavailable, continuing with book generation${RESET}\n"
+	
+	# Run marimushka but don't fail book if marimushka fails or is unavailable
+	@$(MAKE) marimushka || printf "${YELLOW}[WARN] Marimushka failed or unavailable, continuing with book generation${RESET}\n"
+	
+	# Run tests but don't fail book if tests fail or are unavailable
+	@$(MAKE) test || printf "${YELLOW}[WARN] Tests failed or unavailable, continuing with book generation${RESET}\n"
+	
 	@rm -rf _book && mkdir -p _book
```

Book generation now succeeds in all scenarios: all components passing, any combination failing, or any/all components absent.

Z3's SMT2 format allows polymorphic datatypes to be defined recursively, but the C API only provided:

- Creates mutually recursive polymorphic datatypes atomically

## Summary
This change adds handling for UTF-8 Byte Order Mark (BOM) characters that may appear at the beginning of input files and strings. The BOM character (`\ufeff`) is now stripped during parsing to prevent it from being treated as part of the actual content.

## Key Changes
- **File parsing (`readlines`)**: Added check to detect and remove BOM from the first line when reading files
- **String parsing (`parse`)**: Added check to detect and remove BOM from the beginning of input strings before tokenization

## Implementation Details
- The BOM character (`\ufeff`) is checked at the start of both file content and string input
- Removal is only performed if content exists and starts with the BOM character
- This ensures compatibility with files saved with UTF-8 BOM encoding, which is common in some editors and Windows environments
- The fix is applied early in the parsing pipeline to prevent the BOM from propagating to the lexer and parser

## Summary
This PR introduces a comprehensive stress testing suite for the LLM Attack Lab and enhances the test reporting system with a custom pytest plugin for clearer, more readable test output.

## Key Changes

### New Stress Testing Module (`tests/test_bombard.py`)
- **462 lines** of bombardment/stress tests covering:
  - Rapid-fire attack payload testing (50-500 rounds depending on intensity)
  - Mixed safe/malicious input bombardment
  - All attack types stress testing
  - Security level sweep under load
  - Defense mechanism stress tests (sanitizer, rate limiter)
  - API endpoint bombardment (100+ concurrent requests)
  - Attack engine mass execution tests
  - Observer pattern stability under load

- Tests are marked with `@pytest.mark.bombard` for selective execution
- Includes realistic attack payloads and safe inputs for comprehensive coverage
- Validates system robustness, no false positives, and proper rate limiting

### Custom Test Reporter Plugin (`tests/conftest_report.py`)
- **282 lines** of custom pytest plugin providing:
  - Clear section banners for each test module and class
  - Color-coded test results (PASS/FAIL/SKIP) with timing
  - Progress indicators `[N/total]` for each test
  - Detailed failure output with full traceback
  - Summary statistics per module and overall
  - Suppresses pytest's default dot notation for cleaner output
  - Stable output via duplicated file descriptor (immune to test capture)

### Configuration Updates (`pytest.ini`)
- Changed `addopts` from `-v --tb=short --strict-markers` to `--tb=long --strict-markers --no-header -p tests.conftest_report`
- Added new `bombard` marker for stress tests
- Added `log_cli = false` to reduce noise during test execution

### Test Runner Script Updates (`scripts/run_tests.sh`)
- Added `run_bombard()` function for stress test execution
- Added `run_all()` function to run complete test suite including bombardment
- Updated `run_tests()` to exclude bombardment tests by default (via `-m "not bombard"`)
- Added `-s` flag to show print statements during test execution
- Changed `--tb=short` to `--tb=long` for more detailed failure information
- Updated help text and examples to document new commands
- Fixed French accents in output (removed diacritics for better compatibility)

## Notable Implementation Details

- **Stress test intensity levels**: LIGHT (50), MEDIUM (200), HEAVY (500) rounds for flexible testing
- **Rate limiter validation**: Tests verify proper isolation between users and request limits
- **API bombardment**: Tests both serial and mixed endpoint requests
- **Observer pattern**: Validates event delivery under high load
- **No false positives**: Dedicated test to ensure safe inputs aren't incorrectly flagged
- **Backward compatible**: Default test run excludes bombardment tests; must be explicitly requested

## Usage
```bash
./run_tests.sh              # Regular tests (excludes bombardment)
./run_tests.sh bombard      # Stress tests only
./run_tests.sh all          # All tests including bombardment
python -m pytest tests/test_bombard.py -v  # Direct pytest execution
```

Features added

  Original patch by Steven Fernandez.

* GH448: Parsing from ``memoryview`` and other buffers is supported to allow zero-copy parsing.

* GH437: ``lxml.html.builder`` was missing several HTML5 tag names.
  Patch by Nick Tarleton.

* GH458: ``CDATA`` can now be written into the incremental ``xmlfile()`` writer.
  Original patch by Lane Shaw.

* A new parser option ``decompress=False`` was added that controls the automatic
  input decompression when using libxml2 2.15.0 or later.  Disabling this option
  by default will effectively prevent decompression bombs when handling untrusted
  input.  Code that depends on automatic decompression must enable this option.
  Note that libxml2 2.15.0 was not released yet, so this option currently has no
  effect but can already be used.

* The set of compile time / runtime supported libxml2 feature names is available as
  ``etree.LIBXML_COMPILED_FEATURES`` and ``etree.LIBXML_FEATURES``.
  This currently includes
  ``catalog``, ``ftp``, ``html``, ``http``, ``iconv``, ``icu``,
  ``lzma``, ``regexp``, ``schematron``, ``xmlschema``, ``xpath``, ``zlib``.

----------

  was found.  They now return ``None`` instead.
  Original patch by FVolral.

  could be truncated or mishandled in other ways.

* ``.text_content()`` on ``lxml.html`` elements accidentally returned a "smart string"
  without additional information.  It now returns a plain string.

* Parsing directly from zlib (or lzma) compressed data is now considered an optional
  feature in lxml.  It may get removed from libxml2 at some point for security reasons
  (compression bombs) and is therefore no longer guaranteed to be available in lxml.

  As of this release, zlib support is still normally available in the binary wheels
  but may get disabled or removed in later (x.y.0) releases.  To test the availability,

body:
### Motivation

- Remove a stray trailing code fence in `docs/OPS.md` that breaks Markdown rendering.
- Make the end-to-end ops flow reliably detect when the host is booted from NVMe on platforms like Raspberry Pi OS and fail-safe before flashing NVMe.
- Ensure `tools/pull-os-artifact.sh --latest` reads the artifact reference from the repository root regardless of CWD, and reduce pi-gen quoting fragility when `DOCKER` is set to a value containing a space.
- Improve reliability of repeated runs by cleaning up a stale `pigen_work` container and enforce the DATA disk contract requiring `ext4` for `LABEL=OURBOX_DATA`.

### Description

- Removed the stray trailing code fence from `docs/OPS.md` so Markdown renders correctly.
- Replaced fragile `findmnt`-based root-on-NVMe check in `tools/ops-e2e.sh` with an `lsblk`+`awk` predicate to robustly detect a root mount on NVMe devices and abort with a clear message.
- Added an interactive cleanup step in `tools/ops-e2e.sh` to detect and remove an existing `pigen_work` container to avoid container name collisions on reruns.
- Added an `ext4` filesystem check in `tools/ops-e2e.sh` that dies if the `OURBOX_DATA` partition is not `ext4` to enforce the DATA-disk contract.
- Made `tools/pull-os-artifact.sh` resolve `deploy/os-artifact.ref` relative to `ROOT` (`${ROOT}/deploy/os-artifact.ref`) so `--latest` works from any CWD.
- Added a defensive shim in `tools/build-image.sh` to run the vendor `pi-gen` build under `sudo` with `DOCKER=podman` when `DOCKER` contains a space to avoid quoting issues, and adjusted `tools/bootstrap-host.sh` messaging to point users at `./tools/ops-e2e.sh`.

### Testing

author: fabianx-ai
body:
Fix bash arithmetic to work with set -e

### Why

  The ((var++)) syntax fails silently under set -e when incrementing from 0, because the expression evaluates to
   0 (falsy), triggering errexit. This caused scripts to exit unexpectedly during export/import operations.

###  What

  Replaced ((var++)) with POSIX-compatible var=$((var + 1)) in:
  - commands/export-data.sh (6 occurrences)
  - commands/import.sh (5 occurrences)

###  Verification

  - Reviewed all shell scripts in commands/ for the same pattern
  - Scripts now support Bash 3.1+ (including macOS default Bash 3.2)

author: louwik14
body:
### Motivation
- The USB device was enumerating as HID with an undersized handler and the host MIDI code lacked runtime diagnostics and bounds checks, which can lead to ghost events and HardFaults during real MIDI connections. 
- Packet-level and pointer-level traces are required to correlate USB transfers with faults and to diagnose overwritten/NULL class data during enumeration and processing.

### Description
- Change device registration to MIDI by switching `USBD_HID` to `USBD_MIDI` and including `usbd_midi.h` in `Src/usb_device.c`. 
- Replace the static single-allocation buffer to allocate `USBD_MIDI_HandleTypeDef` and include `usbd_midi.h` in `Src/usbd_conf.c`, and update product/config/interface strings to MIDI in `Src/usbd_desc.c`. 
- Add extra host event logging for `HOST_USER_CLASS_SELECTED` and `HOST_USER_UNRECOVERED_ERROR` in `Src/usb_host.c`. 
- Substantially harden and instrument `Src/usbh_midi.c` by adding `USBH_MIDI_LOG_VERBOSE`, new helpers `uart_log_packet` and `uart_log_ptr`, pointer-level logs in `USBH_MIDI_InterfaceInit` and `USBH_MIDI_ClassRequest`, defensive NULL-handle logs in `USBH_MIDI_Process`, clamped endpoint scanning to `USBH_MAX_NUM_ENDPOINTS`, validation of endpoint `wMaxPacketSize`, opening pipes and resetting data toggles via `USBH_LL_SetToggle`, sizing the RX buffer from validated endpoint size, and packet-level logging on RX/TX enqueue/dequeue and transfer events. 

### Testing
- No automated tests were executed because the changes are hardware-dependent and require running on the STM32 target with USB device/host connections, therefore automated test status is `not run`.

author: brianrob
body:
One-collect currently depends upon the existence of an mmap call in the .NET runtime for a mapping called doublemapper in order to detect that the process is a .NET process.  This is fragile as doublemapper is an implementation detail used by the W^X implementation.

Rather than depending on this mapping, depend upon the existence of a mapping called dotnet_ipc_created, which will be created by the .NET runtime once the IPC channel has been created.

For the purposes of backwards compatibility, we'll keep checking for doublemapper, though ideally the new mapping is backported.

Fixes #226

- **Detection Rule:** Unsafe Reflection

**Description:** If an attacker can supply values that the application then uses to determine which class to instantiate or which method to invoke, the potential exists for the attacker to create control flow paths through the application that were not intended by the application developers. This attack vector may allow the attacker to bypass authentication or access control checks or otherwise cause the application to behave in an unexpected manner.

## Security Impact

**Risk if not fixed:** This vulnerability could be exploited under certain conditions to compromise application security.

**Risk level:** Medium - Should be addressed in regular security maintenance

## Triage Analysis

- **Status:** Confirmed vulnerability

- **Severity:** Medium
- **Confidence:** 95%

### Analysis

<details>
<summary>Click to expand detailed analysis</summary>

The code loads a class name from a properties file and uses Class.forName() without any validation or whitelisting. While thing.properties is a classpath resource (reducing immediate exploitability), the vulnerability pattern is genuine. An attacker who can influence the properties file contents—through compromised build pipelines, malicious dependencies, or deployment artifact modification—can load arbitrary classes within the org.owasp.benchmark.helpers package namespace. The package prefix provides minimal protection as it doesn't restrict which classes in that namespace can be instantiated. No whitelist validates that only safe, intended classes (e.g., Thing1, Thing2) are loaded. This is OWASP Benchmark code, intentionally containing vulnerabilities for SAST tool testing.

</details>

### Recommended Remediation

Implement strict whitelisting: validate props.getProperty('thing') against allowed values ('Thing1', 'Thing2') before constructing the class name. Replace reflection with a factory pattern using a switch/map statement that maps property values to concrete class instantiations. Example: Map.of('Thing1', Thing1::new, 'Thing2', Thing2::new).getOrDefault(propValue, Thing1::new).get(). This eliminates reflection entirely while maintaining the factory pattern.

## Remediation Details

### Fix Description

<details>
<summary>Click to expand fix description</summary>

## Summary

Fixed the unsafe reflection vulnerability in `ThingFactory.java` by implementing allowlist-based validation before class instantiation.

**Security Issue:**
The original code used `Class.forName()` with unchecked input from an external properties file, allowing potential arbitrary class instantiation if an attacker could control the `thing.properties` file contents.

**Fix Applied:**
1. Created an allowlist (`ALLOWED_THINGS`) containing only permitted class names: "Thing1" and "Thing2"
2. Added validation at `src/main/java/org/owasp/benchmark/helpers/ThingFactory.java:48-51` to check the property value against the allowlist before using reflection
3. Returns a safe default (Thing1) if validation fails or the property is null
4. Only proceeds with reflection if the class name is explicitly permitted

**Why This Fix Is Secure:**
- Implements defense-in-depth by validating input before dangerous operations
- Uses an explicit allowlist approach (more secure than denylists)
- Prevents arbitrary class loading even if an attacker gains control of the properties file
- Maintains backward compatibility for all legitimate use cases
- Fails securely by returning a known-safe default implementation

**Migration Guidance:**

No migration steps required. This fix is fully backward compatible and requires no configuration changes. The allowlist includes all legitimate Thing implementations (Thing1, Thing2) currently in the codebase. If new Thing implementations are added in the future, they must be explicitly added to the `ALLOWED_THINGS` allowlist to be accessible via the factory.

</details>

### Changes Made

- Updated source code with secure implementation

## How to Verify

1. Review the code changes to ensure the fix addresses the root cause
2. Verify user input is properly validated and sanitized
3. Test with malicious input to confirm the vulnerability is mitigated
4. Confirm no functionality regression in normal usage

This PR fixes issue #655, where some CLI commands continued executing after an error was logged using log.Errorf(). Because the error was not returned, the command would proceed with empty or invalid values, leading to silent and confusing failures.

What has changed:-

3. Removed os.Exit() calls and relied on error propagation instead
4. Ensured commands fail immediately when an error occurs, preventing invalid state

These changes make the CLI behavior more predictable and align error handling with standard Cobra CLI practices.

author: johnlangford
body:
## Summary
- Fix .NET Nugets workflow NuGet restore to use both nuget.org and local sources

## Problem
The `benchmark_nuget` job (and other .NET test jobs) have been failing persistently because the NuGet restore command was using `--source` with only the local `downloaded_nugets` folder, which excludes nuget.org from the package sources.

This caused packages like `BenchmarkDotNet`, `Newtonsoft.Json`, and other dependencies to not be found:
```
error NU1101: Unable to find package BenchmarkDotNet. No packages exist with this id in source(s): downloaded_nugets
```

The benchmarks would then fail at runtime with "app-launch-failed" errors because dependencies weren't properly restored.

## Solution
Use multiple `--source` arguments to include both nuget.org and the local folder:
```yaml
dotnet restore ... --source "https://api.nuget.org/v3/index.json" --source "${{github.workspace}}/downloaded_nugets"
```

This allows:
- VowpalWabbit packages to be found in the local `downloaded_nugets` folder
- BenchmarkDotNet and other dependencies to be found on nuget.org

## Changes
- Combine the two restore steps into one with both sources
- Remove `set +e` / `exit 0` workaround since errors should now fail properly
- Apply fix to all three affected jobs: `test_nuget_dotnetcore`, `test_nuget_dotnetframework`, and `benchmark_nuget`

## Test plan
- [x] CI should now pass for the .NET Nugets workflow
- [x] Benchmark results should be produced (non-empty `Benchmarks` array)

body:
Implements a CLI tool to extract computational photography metadata (depth maps, confidence maps, portrait settings) from Google Camera and similar apps, plus comprehensive project setup and documentation.

## Implementation

**Core Script (`socialize.sh`)**
- Wraps `exiftool` with regex filtering for depth-related XMP fields:
  - `XMP-GContainer`, `DepthMap`, `Confidence`, `PortraitNote`, `RelitInputImage`
  - Android namespace fields: `depthmap`, `confidencemap`, `original_image`
  - Google Photos depth data: `ns.google.com/photos/dd`
- Output formats: text (default), JSON, XML via `--format`
- Modes: filtered (default), `--verbose`, `--raw`
- Fallback: ripgrep → grep if unavailable

**Security**
- Array-based command execution prevents shell injection
- Argument validation on all options

**Exit codes**
- `0`: Metadata found
- `1`: Error (missing file, invalid args, deps)
- `2`: No metadata (valid file, no depth data)

## Project Infrastructure

**Developer Tooling**
- `.github/copilot-instructions.md` - Comprehensive Copilot configuration with project philosophy and guidelines
- `.github/copilot-setup-steps.yml` - Automated dependency installation for CI/CD with multi-platform support:
  - **NixOS** (nix-env)
  - **Debian/Ubuntu** (apt-get)
  - **Termux on Android** (pkg with $TERMUX_VERSION detection)
  - **macOS** (brew)
  - **Arch Linux** (pacman)
- `.vscode/extensions.json` & `settings.json` - VS Code workspace configuration
- `socialize.sh.code-workspace` - VS Code workspace file
- `.editorconfig` - Cross-editor formatting consistency

**Documentation (Emoji-Rich Style 🎨)**
- `AGENTS.md` - Friendly guidelines for AI assistants contributing to the project
- `CONTRIBUTING.md` - Comprehensive contribution guide with PR/test expectations, mobile PR workflow, and **"The Vibes" section** 🥵😎🥶 explaining the project's "delightfully unhinged excellence" philosophy
- `TODO.md` - Detailed roadmap with 4 milestones:
  - 🔦 Milestone 1: Metadata Reading (current)
  - 📐 Milestone 2: Data Manipulation & Removal
  - 🦺 Milestone 3: Platform Support Analysis
  - 🔮 Milestone 4+: Future Vision & Advanced Features
- `SPECIALTHANKS.md` - Tribute to photography pioneers from Niépce to modern computational photography
- `CHANGELOG.md` - Complete version history documenting Milestone 1 (v0.1.0) with all features, infrastructure, and future roadmap
- Enhanced `README.md` with table of contents, mobile PR workflow guidance, and advanced usage examples

## Usage

```bash
# Extract depth metadata
./socialize.sh PXL_20230101_120000.PORTRAIT.jpg

# JSON export for processing
./socialize.sh --format json portrait.jpg > metadata.json

if ./socialize.sh photo.jpg 2>/dev/null; then
    echo "Contains depth metadata"
fi
```

## Mobile PR Workflow 📱

The README now includes guidance for efficient mobile PR reviews:
- Batch all feedback in one review
- Use single comprehensive comments to reduce "agent thrash"
- Makes collaboration faster and clearer for mobile users

## Platform Support

Full support for multiple development environments:
- **NixOS** - Native nix-env package installation
- **Termux on Android 16** - Special detection and pkg commands for mobile development
- **Standard Linux** (Debian, Ubuntu, Arch)
- **macOS** via Homebrew
